Abstract
This study investigated the in£uence of colour of light (‘warm’,‘cool’and arti¢cial‘daylight’white lighting) on
subjects’self-reported mood, cognitive performance and room light estimation. Although no direct e¡ect on
positive and negative mood was indicated, a main e¡ect of gender on several room light estimation dimen-
sions showed that females perceived the room light, across all light settings, as more expressive than did
males. Cognitive taskdata revealed ¢ndings not earlier indicatedby thebehavioural lighting research.Main
